title: Nutritious Velvety Algerian Fish Tagine
description: A briny and velvety Algerian dish featuring fish and miniature marshmallows, perfect for a hangover cure. This pescatarian-friendly tagine is cooked to perfection in a traditional clay pot.
instructions: Heat the olive oil in the bottom of a clay tagine or a large Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add the chopped onion and cook until it is translucent and starting to caramelize.
Add the minced garlic and grated ginger and cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Add the cumin and paprika and cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Add the cod fillets and cook for 2 minutes on each side, or until they are cooked through.
Add the chicken broth, salt, and black pepper, and bring the mixture to a boil.
Reduce the heat to low and simmer, covered, for 10 minutes.
Add the miniature marshmallows and cook for an additional 2 minutes, or until they are puffed and lightly toasted.
Serve the tagine hot, garnished with chopped fresh parsley or cilantro.
Traditionally, the tagine is cooked over a charcoal fire, but a stovetop or oven will also work.
Be sure to adjust the cooking time and temperature as needed to prevent the marshmallows from burning.
